page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.13xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8269CY processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 52 dedicated vCPUs paired with 96.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core allocation of approximately 1.85 GB per vCPU. It operates without hardware GPU accelerators, directing all available host capacity toward general processor execution.

Networking and I/O infrastructure for the ecs.c6.13xlarge is configured with a 12 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The instance does not include integrated local storage, requiring attached network-based block storage volumes for persistent data and operating system installations. Additionally, no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned directly by default.

Due to its high vCPU count relative to RAM capacity, this server profile offers cost efficiency for CPU-bound applications that do not require large per-core memory footprints. The lack of onboard local disks requires dependence on network storage latency and throughput. Typical workloads suited for this configuration include parallel batch processing, distributed build environments, CPU-heavy scientific modeling, web application clusters, and video transcoding.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.13xlarge is a compute-optimized instance hosted on the KVM hypervisor. Driven by an Intel Xeon 8269CY x86_64 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, it supplies 52 dedicated vCPUs and 96.0 GB of system memory, resulting in roughly 1.85 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance features a 12 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, operates without GPU accelerators, and includes zero local disk storage, necessitating external network storage for file systems and runtime data. By offering high core density at a low memory-to-vCPU ratio, the architecture provides qualitative cost advantages for execution environments constrained by CPU rather than memory capacity. The ecs.c6.13xlarge is tailored for parallelized computing workloads, including batch computational tasks, continuous integration and compilation pipelines, backend application servers, and media encoding.
